carriage.material: Ti-6Al-4V carriage, hardened steel arbors, brass balance
carriage.poise_note: POISING IS THE SINGLE MOST CRITICAL ASSEMBLY OPERATION.  The un-poised first moment computed above (72.78 g-mm) produces a gravity torque 1x larger than the torque available at the escape wheel, so the carriage will not run until it is poised to the specification below.  Correct it by (1) a screwed counter-mass in the lower carriage plate at 180 deg from the balance, or (2) removing material from the escape-wheel side of the rim band.  Verify on a poising tool / roller jeweller, not in CAD.

escapement.type: Swiss lever, club-tooth escape wheel, 15 teeth
escapement.reason_for_choice: The Swiss lever is the only escapement with (a) self-locked detent action that does not need a detent spring, (b) a documented geometry that can be laid out from tooth counts and angles, and (c) proven behaviour inside a rotating carriage.  A detent (chronometer) escapement was rejected because it is not self-starting and would need an auxiliary starting spring inside the carriage.  A Potter / fixed-ring escapement was rejected because it removes the fixed fourth wheel and therefore removes the 1 rpm kinematic closure this design relies on.
escapement.escape_wheel_material: hardened 1.4034 steel, wire-EDM then lapped impulse faces
escapement.manufacturability: The escape wheel and the pallet stones CANNOT be reliably 3-D printed: the impulse faces need a surface finish better than Ra 0.2 um and a hardness above 60 HRC, otherwise the lever will not unlock consistently.  Model them, but source them as wire-EDM / laser-cut hardened steel (see BOM_BOUGHT / BOM_MADE).

validation.check: both members of every mesh use ONE conjugate tooth system, and no member is undercut
validation.detail: z_min(20 deg) = 17.10.  Every mesh of this train contains a pinion with z <= 16, so EVERY mesh is cycloidal, with one describing circle shared by both members (rr = m*z_pinion/4, which makes each pinion flank an exactly radial hypocycloid -- the classical watch pinion leaf).  Mixing an involute wheel with a cycloidal pinion would NOT be conjugate and the velocity ratio would not be constant.  Meshes: Barrel gear/Great wheel rr=4.9000; Great pinion/Centre wheel rr=1.5000; Centre pinion/Intermediate wheel rr=1.5000; Intermediate pinion/Carriage rim gear rr=2.1000; Fixed fourth wheel/Escape pinion rr=1.1250; Canon pinion/Minute wheel rr=2.8800; Minute pinion/Hour wheel rr=3.6000.  Undeclared undercut: none.  Mixed systems: none.
